 By Lori Riley | lriley@courant.com | Hartford Courant PUBLISHED: October 19, 2026 at 6:00 AM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... STORRS – Last year, the UConn women’s basketball team played Southern Connecticut in one of their two exhibition games. Two years ago, the Huskies played Fort Hays State in the preseason.
 This year, because of new NCAA rules governing exhibition games, the caliber of the Huskies’ exhibition opponents has increased dramatically. UConn faced Syracuse in its first exhibition last week, winning 88-60, and will play Texas, a Final Four team the last two years, Monday at PeoplesBank Arena in another high-level preseason game that doesn’t count.
 “You just want to get out on the court like we did the other day and kind of get a feel – ‘Is what we see every day in practice, is that real, is that pretend, are we better than that, are we worse than that? What things do we struggle with?’ ” UConn coach Geno Auriemma said Saturday.
 “Then you want to try to get a team to play against that can challenge you in different areas and I’m sure they’re thinking the same thing – in a non-threatening situation – and you go to practice the next week and you have a much clearer picture of what you want to work on.
 “I think you’re going to see more of these high-profile exhibition games.”
 Texas went 35-4 and advanced to the Final Four in Phoenix last season, losing to eventual champ UCLA 51-44 in the semifinals. The Longhorns, coached by Vic Schaefer, will play in their first exhibition game of the season. They are ranked ninth in the ESPN Preseason Top 25 poll and were picked to finish second in the SEC behind South Carolina.
 Texas forward Madison Booker (35) works against Michigan guard Te'yala Delfosse (33) during the Elite Eight of the NCAA college basketball tournament, Sunday, March 29, 2026, in Fort Worth, Texas. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez) 
 Texas returns senior Madison Booker , who was named to the All-SEC first team and is 31 points away from reaching 2,000 in her career. Texas’ second-leading scorer from last year, guard Jordan Lee , who averaged 13 ppg, transferred to South Carolina.
 Auriemma said that junior guard Allie Ziebell, who had an ankle injury and was not available for the first exhibition game, will be ready to play Monday but that the other two injured UConn players – Blanca Quinonez (shoulder) and Marine Dursus (foot) – have not been cleared to play yet.
 “So far they’ve been able to do more drill stuff than they did before,” Auriemma said of Quinonez and Dursus. “It’s been encouraging to see them actually doing more things than they were doing before.”
 What to know
 Site: PeoplesBank Arena, Hartford.
 Time/date: 7 p.m., Monday
 TV: WFSB
 Streaming: UConn+
 Radio: UConn Sports Network on FOX Sports 97.9
